sources.note: Cited second-hand as the only reported six-level level-tone system (Dihoff 1977); a five-level reanalysis is said to be possible (Odden 1995). No inventory labels or data given here.

tone.quote: Level-tone systems have two to five levels of relative pitch: L(ow) vs. H(igh); L vs. M(id) vs. H; L vs. M vs. H vs T(op); or B(ottom) vs. L vs. M vs. H vs. T. Systems with two levels are most widespread; systems with more than three levels are relatively uncommon (Bariba: Welmers 1952; Bench, a.k.a. Gimira: Wedekind 1983, 1985). One single case of six-level system has been reported: Chori (Dihoff 1977), for which reanalysis as a five-level system is possible (Odden 1995). These languages are spoken in Subsaharan Africa, a domain where level tones are especially common.
